ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early-termination charge applies. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

input.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives only for-cause, insolvency and performance-based termination rights, and Section 2.1 expressly denies any termination right across a three-year term. We need a convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; our fallback is 60-90 days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.
input.summary: Add a Customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid Fees.

ops.oldText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
ops.newText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction.

input.comment: [Playbook] Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts fall outside our accepted list and directly conflict with Section 28.2, which already gives exclusive jurisdiction to the New York County courts. We have aligned Section 28.1 with New York law and venue; Delaware, California or England and Wales would also work.
input.summary: Replace Singapore law/venue with New York law and New York County courts.

ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in each Deliverable upon creation. To the extent any such assignment is ineffective, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, transferable licence to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverable for Customer's business.

input.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for: Deliverables are created specifically for us, so Vendor ownership with only a revocable, term-limited licence is not acceptable (and sits oddly with the perpetual licence in Section 13.2). We have reversed the assignment and added a licence-back fallback; Vendor Technology remains Vendor's under Section 14.3.
input.summary: Give Customer ownership of Deliverables with a perpetual licence fallback.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer's only purchase commitment is the amount stated in the applicable Order Form for the current twelve-month term, which Customer may reduce on thirty days' written notice. Any shortfall is settled by a true-up invoice for the unmet committed amount, and no penalty or take-or-pay charge applies. This Section does not limit Customer's termination rights.

input.comment: [Playbook] A three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right is a walk-away for us, and it contradicts Section 12.3's acknowledgement that no minimum-volume commitment has been made. We have limited any commitment to the current 12-month term, made it reducible on 30 days' notice, and replaced the penalty with a true-up.
input.summary: Limit the commitment to 12 months, reducible on notice, with a true-up instead of take-or-pay.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty days, return or export all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention, and certify such deletion in writing.

input.comment: [Playbook] The agreement contains no exit obligations: Section 10.1 assumes a transition period that is never granted, and Section 16.5 points Customer Data to a Section 11 that does not exist. We have inserted our standard transition-assistance, data-return and deletion-certification paragraph (fallback: 90 days of assistance).
input.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return within 30 days and certified deletion.
